claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Gallagher et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Diazaborine is an inhibitor of the essential Drg1 AAA-ATPase that rapidly blocks mid-late steps of 60S subunit maturation.
claims.source: Diazaborine, an inhibitor of the essential Drg1 AAA-ATPase, rapidly blocks mid-late steps of 60S subunit maturation (Loibl et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Loibl et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The RQC binds to 60S ribosomal subunits containing stalled polypeptides and leads to their degradation.
claims.source: A pioneering study reported that a set of proteins termed the RQC binds to 60S ribosomal subunits containing stalled polypeptides and leads to their degradation.
claims.evidence: Refers to a pioneering study, implicitly citing previous work.

claims.claim: The RQC triggers a specific stress signal that leads to Hsf1 target gene activation.
claims.source: In the process, the RQC triggers a specific stress signal that leads to Hsf1 target gene activation (Brandman et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Brandman et al., 2012.

claims.claim: Cells lacking Tae2 fail to activate Hsf1 following translational stress.
claims.source: Thus, cells lacking a component of the RQC, the Tae2 protein, fail to activate Hsf1 following translational stress.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the RQC pathway.

claims.claim: Activation of Hsf1 target genes and downregulation of RP genes following Top1/2 depletion is unaffected by deletion of TAE2.
claims.source: We found that activation of two Hsf1 target genes (SSA1 and HSP42) and downregulation of two RP genes (RPL30 and RPL39) was unaffected by deletion of TAE2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) and conclude that RQC does not play a role in RASTR.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claims.claim: RQC does not play a role in RASTR.
claims.source: and conclude that RQC does not play a role in RASTR.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental results with tae2 deletion.

claims.claim: Cells have developed distinct mechanisms to adapt the Hsf1 transcriptional program to defects in both ribosome activity and ribosome assembly.
claims.source: These results highlight that cells have developed distinct mechanisms to adapt the Hsf1 transcriptional program to defects in both ribosome activity and ribosome assembly.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from experimental results.

claims.claim: Ifh1 association with RP gene promoters in growing cells is rapidly disrupted (within 5 min) following inhibition of TORC1 kinase by rapamycin.
claims.source: We reported previously that the association of Ifh1 with RP gene promoters in growing cells is rapidly disrupted (within 5 min) following inhibition of the growth-promoting TORC1 kinase by addition of rapamycin to the medium (Schawalder et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Schawalder et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Stable release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters (measured 20 min after rapamycin addition) requires its C-terminal domain together with a complex of proteins containing casein kinase 2 (CK2) and two RiBi factors, Utp22 and Rrp7.
claims.source: More recently (Albert et al., 2016), we found that stable release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters (measured 20 min after rapamycin addition) requires its C-terminal domain together with a complex of proteins containing casein kinase 2 (CK2) and two RiBi factors, Utp22 and Rrp7, with which Ifh1 interacts to form the CURI complex (Rudra et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Albert et al., 2016 and Rudra et al., 2007.

claims.claim: In ifh1-ΔC cells, the truncated protein is rapidly released but later returns to RP gene promoters following TORC1 inhibition.
claims.source: Thus, in ifh1-ΔC cells the truncated protein is rapidly released but later returns to RP gene promoters following TORC1 inhibition.
claims.evidence: Based on previous experimental observations.

claims.claim: ifh1-ΔC promoter release is stable following Top1 depletion.
claims.source: Interestingly, ifh1-ΔC promoter release is stable following Top1 depletion, suggesting that an unknown mechanism regulates Ifh1 during RASTR (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: RP gene repression and Hsf1 target gene activation occur with identical kinetics following RASTR activation.
claims.source: The fact that RP gene repression and Hsf1 target gene activation occur with identical kinetics following RASTR activation (Figure 3B), and that Ifh1 concentrates in nuclear foci rapidly after topoisomerase depletion (Figure 3C), suggests that Ifh1 could be sensitive to the accumulation of unassembled RPs in the nucleus, as is presumably the case for Hsf1.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claims.claim: Ifh1 concentrates in nuclear foci rapidly after topoisomerase depletion.
claims.source: The fact that RP gene repression and Hsf1 target gene activation occur with identical kinetics following RASTR activation (Figure 3B), and that Ifh1 concentrates in nuclear foci rapidly after topoisomerase depletion (Figure 3C), suggests that Ifh1 could be sensitive to the accumulation of unassembled RPs in the nucleus, as is presumably the case for Hsf1.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: In cells lacking Tom1, Ifh1 accumulates in prominent nuclear foci even in the absence of stress.
claims.source: To begin with, in cells lacking Tom1, an E3 ligase required for degradation of unassembled RPs (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b), but not in TOM1 cells, Ifh1 accumulates in prominent nuclear foci even in the absence of stress (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citations.

claims.claim: Tom1 is an E3 ligase required for degradation of unassembled RPs.
claims.source: To begin with, in cells lacking Tom1, an E3 ligase required for degradation of unassembled RPs (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b), but not in TOM1 cells, Ifh1 accumulates in prominent nuclear foci even in the absence of stress (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b.

claims.claim: tom1-Δ is synthetically lethal with ifh1-AA.
claims.source: Remarkably, tom1-Δ is synthetically lethal with ifh1-AA (Figure 3E) supporting the notion that RP aggregation could directly impact on Ifh1 promoter binding.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: tom1-Δ is not synthetically lethal with ifh1-6.
claims.source: Remarkably, tom1-Δ is not synthetically lethal with ifh1-6 (Figure 3E), supporting the notion that genetic interaction with ifh1-AA is directly linked to the ability of Ifh1 to bind RP gene promoters.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: The insoluble fraction following topoisomerase depletion is enriched in chaperones and RPs.
claims.source: As previously reported for tom1-Δ cells (Sung et al., 2016a), the insoluble fraction is enriched in chaperones and RPs (Figure 3F,G).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F,G and citation.

claims.claim: Following topoisomerase depletion, there is a strong increase in RiBi factors in the insoluble fraction, primarily those implicated in biogenesis of the large ribosomal subunit.
claims.source: We also noted a strong increase in RiBi factors, primarily those implicated in biogenesis of the large ribosomal subunit (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Ifh1 was never detected in an insoluble fraction in the absence of stress but was invariably detected in these fractions following topoisomerase depletion.
claims.source: Importantly, Ifh1 was never detected in an insoluble fraction in the absence of stress but was invariably detected in these fractions following topoisomerase depletion (Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data in supplementary file.

claims.claim: Ifh1 binding is highly specific to RP genes.
claims.source: It is important to note that Ifh1 binding is highly specific to RP genes (Knight et al., 2014) and that the transcriptional effect of its nuclear depletion is restricted to RP genes and a very small number of additional targets (Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Knight et al., 2014 and experimental data in supplementary file.

claims.claim: Ifh1 depletion by anchor-away leads to a significant and highly specific decrease in RP gene transcription.
claims.source: it nonetheless leads to a significant and highly specific decrease in RP gene transcription as measured by RNAPII ChIP-seq (Figure 4B; Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Ifh1 depletion leads to aberrant rRNA processing.
claims.source: Interestingly, Ifh1 depletion also leads to aberrant rRNA processing (Figure 4C) as would expected in conditions where RP levels become limiting (Reiter et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to Reiter et al., 2011.

claims.claim: 60 min of Ifh1 anchoring alone causes a significant down-regulation of Hsf1 target genes.
claims.source: Remarkably, we noted that 60 min of Ifh1 anchoring alone, in the absence of topoisomerase depletion, also caused a significant down-regulation of Hsf1 target genes (Figure 4D; Supplementary file 4) even though Ifh1 is absent from the promoters of these genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the Hsf1 transcriptional program is continuously influenced by RP production.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and supplementary figures.

claims.claim: Upregulation of Hsf1 target genes was either abolished or strongly reduced when Top1 or Top1 and Top2 were degraded following nuclear depletion of Ifh1.
claims.source: Consistent with this idea, we found that upregulation of Hsf1 target genes was either abolished or strongly reduced (Figure 4E,F,G; Supplementary file 4) when Top1 or Top1 and Top2 were degraded following nuclear depletion of Ifh1, indicating that RP production is required for Hsf1 target gene activation during RASTR.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E,F,G.

claims.claim: RP production is required for Hsf1 target gene activation during RASTR.
claims.source: indicating that RP production is required for Hsf1 target gene activation during RASTR.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental results with Ifh1 depletion.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide treatment blocks all translational elongations, leading to rapid depletion of the nuclear pools of RPs.
claims.source: As an alternative approach to test the requirement for de novo RP synthesis to initiate RASTR we used cycloheximide treatment, which blocks all translational elongations, thus leading to rapid depletion of the nuclear pools of RPs (Figure 5A; Gorenstein and Warner, 1977; Warner, 1977; Reiter et al., 2011; Lam et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide alone triggers a rapid arrest of rRNA processing.
claims.source: As reported by others (Reiter et al., 2011), we confirmed that cycloheximide alone also triggers a rapid arrest of rRNA processing (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and citation to Reiter et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide treatment triggers a transcriptional response exactly opposite to that induced by RASTR, namely Hsf1 target gene downregulation and RP gene upregulation.
claims.source: Quite strikingly, we observed a transcriptional response to cycloheximide treatment exactly opposite to that induced by RASTR, namely Hsf1 target gene downregulation and RP gene upregulation (Figure 5C; Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Even in unstressed cells RP production may contribute to a basal level of Hsf1 activation while at the same time limiting Ifh1 activity at RP gene promoters.
claims.source: This finding suggests that even in unstressed cells RP production may contribute to a basal level of Hsf1 activation while at the same time limiting Ifh1 activity at RP gene promoters.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from cycloheximide experiments.

claims.claim: Treatment of cells undergoing Top1 or Top1/2 depletion with cycloheximide completely abolished both RP gene repression and activation of Hsf1 target genes.
claims.source: Significantly, treatment of cells undergoing Top1 or Top1/2 depletion with cycloheximide (auxin + CHX) completely abolished both RP gene repression and activation of Hsf1 target genes (Figure 5D,E; Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claims.claim: RASTR is dependent upon de novo protein synthesis.
claims.source: These findings clearly demonstrate that RASTR is dependent upon de novo protein synthesis.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental results with cycloheximide.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide treatment efficiently prevents aggregation of newly synthesized RPs following proteasome inhibition.
claims.source: Importantly, it was recently reported that cycloheximide treatment efficiently prevents aggregation of newly synthesized RPs following proteasome inhibition (Sung et al., 2016a).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Sung et al., 2016a.

claims.claim: CHX treatment leads to strong reduction of Ifh1-eGFP nuclear foci that are observed in cells lacking Tom1.
claims.source: Perhaps as a direct consequence of this, we found that CHX treatment also leads to strong reduction of Ifh1-eGFP nuclear foci that are observed in cells lacking the ubiquitin ligase Tom1, which is specifically required for efficient degradation of unassembled RPs (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure and citations.

claims.claim: Ifh1 dis-aggregation following cycloheximide exposure is associated with increased Ifh1 binding at a RP gene promoter, which becomes significant in tom1-Δ cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, Ifh1 dis-aggregation following cycloheximide exposure is associated with increased Ifh1 binding at a RP gene promoter, which becomes significant in tom1-Δ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide treatment prevents the release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters in response to the activation of RASTR by topoisomerase depletion.
claims.source: Similarly, cycloheximide treatment also prevents the release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters in response to the activation of RASTR by topoisomerase depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claims.claim: There is a large increase in cells that accumulate RP (Rpl25) or Ifh1 nuclear aggregates during RASTR that is abolished in the presence of cycloheximide.
claims.source: Consistent with this view, we observed a large increase in cells that accumulate RP (Rpl25) or Ifh1 nuclear aggregates during RASTR that is abolished in the presence of cycloheximide (Figure 5F,G; Figure 5—figure supplement 1E, F).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F,G and supplementary figures.

claims.claim: Newly synthetized RPs, in both stressed and unstressed cells, operate as a central hub in coordinating the expression of RP genes themselves with the Hsf1-dependent activation of chaperone and proteasome genes.
claims.source: More generally, these data indicate that newly synthetized RPs, in both stressed and unstressed cells, operate as a central hub in coordinating the expression of RP genes themselves with the Hsf1-dependent activation of chaperone and proteasome genes.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental results.

claims.claim: Rapamycin triggers a rapid arrest of rRNA processing.
claims.source: As reported previously, rapamycin triggers a rapid arrest of rRNA processing (Figure 6A) and a decrease of RP and RiBi gene expression (Figure 6B,C; Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Rapamycin causes a decrease of RP and RiBi gene expression.
claims.source: As reported previously, rapamycin triggers a rapid arrest of rRNA processing (Figure 6A) and a decrease of RP and RiBi gene expression (Figure 6B,C; Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claims.claim: Hsf1 target genes are transiently up- and downregulated at 5 and 20 min, respectively, following rapamycin addition.
claims.source: Interestingly, we noted that Hsf1 target genes are transiently up- and downregulated at 5 and 20 min, respectively, following rapamycin addition (Figure 6B,C; Supplementary file 6), suggesting that RASTR is activated at the early time point but shortly thereafter turned off.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claims.claim: RP production ceases around 15 min after rapamycin treatment.
claims.source: Consistent with this view, it has been reported that RP production ceases around 15 min after rapamycin treatment (Reiter et al., 2011), which we suggest would turn off the signal for RASTR, thus explaining the downregulation of Hsf1 target genes observed at 20 min.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Reiter et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide pre-treatment specifically prevented RP gene repression and Hsf1 target gene activation at 5 min following rapamycin addition.
claims.source: Remarkably, this specifically prevented RP gene repression and Hsf1 target gene activation at 5 min following rapamycin addition, whereas at the longer time point (20 min) RP genes and Hsf1 were regulated independently of cycloheximide (Figure 6D,E; Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide pre-treatment prevents release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters at 5 min, but not at 20 min following rapamycin treatment.
claims.source: Consistent with the early block in RP gene downregulation being due to a failure to initiate RASTR immediately following rapamycin addition, we showed that cycloheximide pre-treatment prevents release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters at 5 min, but not at 20 min following rapamycin treatment (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: Regulation of RP gene transcription following TORC1 inactivation by rapamycin operates through two distinct mechanisms at short and long timescales.
claims.source: The effects of rapamycin treatment described above are fully consistent with our previous report demonstrating that regulation of RP gene transcription following TORC1 inactivation by rapamycin operates through two distinct mechanisms at short and long timescales, with the latter dependent on RNAPI activity and the CURI complex (Albert et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Albert et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Heat shock causes strong downregulation of RP genes and upregulation of Hsf1 target genes only 5 min following a shift in temperature to 40°C.
claims.source: As expected, we observed strong downregulation of RP genes and upregulation of Hsf1 target genes only 5 min following a shift in temperature to 40°C (Figure 7A–C, left panels) that was also accompanied by strong upregulation of Msn2 target genes and downregulation of RiBi genes (Figure 7A, left panel).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-C.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide pre-treatment prevents the strong and immediate repression of RP genes following heat shock.
claims.source: Remarkably, though, we found that cycloheximide pre-treatment prevents the strong and immediate repression of RP genes following heat shock (Figure 7A,B; right panels; Supplementary file 6), consistent again with the idea that this facet of the heat-shock response is identical to that which occurs during RASTR.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claims.claim: Hsf1 target genes are still activated following heat shock in the presence of cycloheximide.
claims.source: Importantly though, Hsf1 target genes are still activated following heat shock in the presence of cycloheximide (Figure 7A,C; right panels), presumably because the unfolding of thermo-labile proteins induced by heat shock is alone sufficient to activate Hsf1 even in the absence of continuing RP synthesis.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A,C.

claims.claim: RASTR may constitute the earliest transcriptional response, at the level of RNAPII, to a wide variety of stress conditions.
claims.source: Nevertheless, the striking requirement for de novo protein synthesis for RP gene downregulation following heat shock strongly suggests that RASTR plays an integral role in this component of the heat-shock response and thus may constitute the earliest transcriptional response, at the level of RNAPII, to a wide variety of stress conditions.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from experimental results with heat shock and cycloheximide.

claims.claim: RASTR is a novel regulatory pathway that allows rapid and simultaneous up-regulation of protein homeostasis genes and downregulation of RP genes following disruption of various steps in ribosome biogenesis.
claims.source: In this study, we uncover a novel regulatory pathway, hereafter referred to as the Ribosomal Assembly Stress Response (RASTR), that allows rapid and simultaneous up-regulation of protein homeostasis genes and downregulation of RP genes following disruption of various steps in ribosome biogenesis (rRNA production, processing or RP assembly).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claims.claim: RASTR is highly specific to the RP and Hsf1 regulons, with little or no effect on a much larger group of genes implicated in the Environmental Stress Response (ESR).
claims.source: We show that RASTR is highly specific to the RP and Hsf1 regulons, with little or no effect on a much larger group of genes implicated in the Environmental Stress Response (ESR).
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data comparing different gene groups.

claims.claim: RASTR requires neo-synthesis of RPs following stress.
claims.source: Importantly, RASTR requires neo-synthesis of RPs following stress and is linked to the accumulation of RP aggregates, which we propose lead to Hsf1 activation, through chaperone competition, and to the sequestration of Ifh1 in an insoluble nucleolar fraction.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental results with Ifh1 depletion and cycloheximide.

claims.claim: RASTR is linked to the accumulation of RP aggregates.
claims.source: Importantly, RASTR requires neo-synthesis of RPs following stress and is linked to the accumulation of RP aggregates, which we propose lead to Hsf1 activation, through chaperone competition, and to the sequestration of Ifh1 in an insoluble nucleolar fraction.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data showing RP accumulation in insoluble fractions.

claims.claim: RP aggregates lead to Hsf1 activation through chaperone competition.
claims.source: which we propose lead to Hsf1 activation, through chaperone competition, and to the sequestration of Ifh1 in an insoluble nucleolar fraction.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental observations.

claims.claim: RP aggregates lead to the sequestration of Ifh1 in an insoluble nucleolar fraction.
claims.source: which we propose lead to Hsf1 activation, through chaperone competition, and to the sequestration of Ifh1 in an insoluble nucleolar fraction.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data showing Ifh1 in insoluble fractions.

claims.claim: Protein synthesis inhabitation via cycloheximide treatment leads to a transcriptional response opposite to that of RASTR.
claims.source: Notably, we show that protein synthesis inhabitation via cycloheximide treatment leads to a transcriptional response opposite to that of RASTR, supporting a model in which unstressed cells constantly monitor nuclear levels of unassembled RPs and use this information to balance expression of Hsf1 target genes with those encoding RPs.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data with cycloheximide.

claims.claim: Unstressed cells constantly monitor nuclear levels of unassembled RPs and use this information to balance expression of Hsf1 target genes with those encoding RPs.
claims.source: supporting a model in which unstressed cells constantly monitor nuclear levels of unassembled RPs and use this information to balance expression of Hsf1 target genes with those encoding RPs.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on experimental observations.

claims.claim: RASTR is the initial transcriptional response to inactivation of TORC1 kinase.
claims.source: Finally, we demonstrate that RASTR is the initial transcriptional response to inactivation of TORC1 kinase, supporting a key role for this regulatory pathway in the activation of a protein homeostasis transcriptional program that allows cells to cope with the proteotoxic consequences of disruptions to ribosome biogenesis.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data with rapamycin treatment.

claims.claim: Disequilibrium at any step-in ribosome biogenesis will lead to RASTR activation until the pool of unassembled RPs decreases.
claims.source: Our data indicate that disequilibrium at any step-in ribosome biogenesis (rRNA transcription, early or late rRNA processing or assembly) will lead to RASTR activation until the pool of unassembled RPs decreases.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental results with different perturbations to ribosome biogenesis.

claims.claim: RPs are among the most abundant ubiquitinylated proteins that accumulate in the nucleus of proteasome-deficient S. cerevisiae and human cells.
claims.source: It is important to note that RPs are among the most abundant ubiquitinylated proteins that accumulate in the nucleus of proteasome-deficient S. cerevisiae and human cells (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b; Lam et al., 2007; Mayor et al., 2007), suggesting that the synthesis of RPs and their assembly into ribosomes must be tightly coordinated with the cell's proteostasis capacity.
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Induction of ribosome assembly stress is correlated with the rapid accumulation of RPs in a detergent-insoluble fraction.
claims.source: Consistent with this view, we show here that induction of ribosome assembly stress is correlated with the rapid accumulation of RPs in a detergent-insoluble fraction and that blocking de novo RP production, either by anchoring away Ifh1 or treating cells with cycloheximide, diminishes or abolishes a key transcriptional consequence of RASTR, namely upregulation of Hsf1 target genes.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data.

claims.claim: Blocking de novo RP production diminishes or abolishes upregulation of Hsf1 target genes during RASTR.
claims.source: and that blocking de novo RP production, either by anchoring away Ifh1 or treating cells with cycloheximide, diminishes or abolishes a key transcriptional consequence of RASTR, namely upregulation of Hsf1 target genes.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data with Ifh1 depletion and cycloheximide.

claims.claim: RP aggregates are an important activating signal for RASTR.
claims.source: Our observations thus strongly suggest that RP aggregates are an important activating signal for RASTR.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental results.

claims.claim: A large number of additional proteins accumulate in an insoluble fraction upon ribosome assembly stress, including many RiBi proteins, the RP gene activator Ifh1, and chaperones.
claims.source: Nevertheless, we and others (Sung et al., 2016a) detect a large number of additional proteins that accumulate in an insoluble fraction upon ribosome assembly stress, including many RiBi proteins (e.g. numerous rRNA helicases and processing factors), the RP gene activator Ifh1, and chaperones.
claims.evidence: Based on experimental data and citation.

claims.claim: RP- and Ifh1-containing aggregates are highly dynamic.
claims.source: In any event, our data suggest that RP- and Ifh1-containing aggregates are highly dynamic since the promoter release of Ifh1 and activation of Hsf1 following Top1 degradation are rapidly reversed by Top2 compensation (Figure 1) and Ifh1 aggregates that appear in tom1-Δ cells quickly diminish following cycloheximide treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Based on experimental observations.

claims.claim: Nucleolar proteins can form sub-compartmental structures by promoting liquid-liquid phase separation.
claims.source: Interestingly, it has recently been reported that nucleolar proteins can form sub-compartmental structures by promoting liquid-liquid phase separation (Berry et al., 2015; Feric et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Berry et al., 2015; Feric et al., 2016.

claims.claim: In strains where RNAPI is constitutively active, Ifh1 is released from RP gene promoters shortly after TORC1 inhibition by rapamycin treatment (~5 min) but returns only 15 min later.
claims.source: We showed previously (Albert et al., 2016) that in strains where RNAPI is constitutively active (Laferté et al., 2006) Ifh1 is released from RP gene promoters shortly after TORC1 inhibition by rapamycin treatment (~5 min) but returns only 15 min later.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Albert et al., 2016 and Laferté et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Two RiBi proteins (Utp22 and Rrp7) can sequester Ifh1 in the CURI complex.
claims.source: This promoter re-binding does not occur in wild-type cells due to the action of two RiBi proteins (Utp22 and Rrp7) that can sequester Ifh1 in the CURI (Casein Kinase 2/Utp22/Rrp7/Ifh1) complex (Albert et al., 2016; Rudra et al., 2007) allowing to re-align RP gene expression with RNAPI activity.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Albert et al., 2016; Rudra et al., 2007.

claims.claim: S. cerevisiae has developed temporally distinct mechanisms to regulate RP gene expression.
claims.source: These findings revealed that S. cerevisiae has developed temporally distinct mechanisms to regulate RP gene expression.
claims.evidence: Based on previous findings cited in the text.

claims.claim: The short timescale mechanism of RP gene regulation results from a rapid rise in unassembled RPs that occurs immediately following TORC1 inhibition, or other stresses that disrupt ribosome assembly.
claims.source: One of the keys finding in the present study is to confirm the existence of a two-step process in RP gene regulation and to link the first step to control of the Hsf1 regulon. We propose that this short timescale mechanism results from a rapid rise in unassembled RPs that occurs immediately following TORC1 inhibition, or other stresses that disrupt ribosome assembly, such as depletion of Top1 or RiBi factors.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental findings.

claims.claim: The rapid induction of Hsf1 target genes, in combination with the arrest of RP gene transcription, contributes to the eventual clearing of proteotoxic unassembled RPs from the nucleus.
claims.source: Following ribosome assembly stress, we imagine that the rapid induction of Hsf1 target genes, in combination with the arrest of RP gene transcription, contributes to the eventual clearing of proteotoxic unassembled RPs from the nucleus, thereby removing the signal that promotes RASTR and leads to Ifh1 promoter release and Hsf1 activation.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental observations.

claims.claim: Ribosome assembly stress in higher eukaryotes has been studied extensively in the context of ribosomopathies.
claims.source: As alluded to above, ribosome assembly stress in higher eukaryotes has been studied extensively in the context of ribosomopathies, diseases often associated with RP gene haplo-insufficiencies, RP gene point mutations or mutations in RiBi factors.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosomopathies.

claims.claim: Unassembled RPs trigger a feedback mechanism that decreases transcription of ribosome biogenesis genes by inhibiting c-Myc function and arrests cell growth through p53 activation.
claims.source: One hypothesis put forward to explain these observations is that unassembled RPs trigger a feedback mechanism that decreases transcription of ribosome biogenesis genes by inhibiting c-Myc function and arrests cell growth through p53 activation (Dai et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Dai et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2016.

claims.claim: The rRNA helicase DDX21 binds to and activates RP gene promoters in a manner that may be sensitive to the status of ribosome biogenesis.
claims.source: It has also been recently reported that the rRNA helicase DDX21 binds to and activates RP gene promoters in a manner that may be sensitive to the status of ribosome biogenesis (Calo et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Calo et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Unassembled RPs could mediate an ancestral process to regulate ribosome biogenesis conserved from prokaryotes to eukaryotes.
claims.source: Taken together, these findings suggest that unassembled RPs could mediate an ancestral process to regulate ribosome biogenesis conserved from prokaryotes (Nomura, 1999) to eukaryotes.
claims.evidence: Based on inference from multiple findings and citation to Nomura, 1999.

claims.claim: Hsf1 is a key sensor of proteotoxic stress in all eukaryotes that controls a common set of chaperones conserved from yeast to human.
claims.source: Hsf1 is a key sensor of proteotoxic stress in all eukaryotes that controls a common set of chaperones conserved from yeast to human.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about Hsf1.

claims.claim: Hsf1 reduces protein aggregate formation leading to neurogenerative diseases.
claims.source: One protective function reported for Hsf1 is its ability to reduce protein aggregate formation leading to neurogenerative diseases (Neef et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Neef et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Hsf1 exerts a pro-oncogenic function through its ability to promote proteostasis in rapidly growing tumor cells.
claims.source: On the other hand, Hsf1 also exerts a pro-oncogenic function through its ability to promote proteostasis in rapidly growing tumor cells (Mendillo et al., 2012; Santagata et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Mendillo et al., 2012; Santagata et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Hsf1 activity is tightly linked to ribosome biogenesis in yeast, in a manner independent of the RQC mechanism.
claims.source: Our work and that of Tye et al. (2018) demonstrates that Hsf1 activity is tightly linked to ribosome biogenesis in yeast, in a manner independent of the previously described RQC mechanism that contributes to the dissociation of aberrant nascent polypeptides from the ribosome (Brandman et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Based on experimental findings from this study and citation to Tye et al., 2018 and Brandman et al., 2012.

claims.claim: RPs are subjected to a high turnover rate compared to other nuclear components in mammalian cells.
claims.source: Although it is currently unknown if RASTR is conserved in metazoans, we note that RPs are also subjected to a high turnover rate compared to other nuclear components in mammalian cells and that proteasome or ribosome assembly inhibition trigger a rapid accumulation of RPs in the nucleus, whereas arrest of translation has an opposite effect (Sung et al., 2016a; Lam et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Sung et al., 2016a; Lam et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Proteasome or ribosome assembly inhibition trigger a rapid accumulation of RPs in the nucleus in mammalian cells, whereas arrest of translation has an opposite effect.
claims.source: and that proteasome or ribosome assembly inhibition trigger a rapid accumulation of RPs in the nucleus, whereas arrest of translation has an opposite effect (Sung et al., 2016a; Lam et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Sung et al., 2016a; Lam et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Cycloheximide treatment abolishes Hsf1 activity in mammalian cells by an unknown mechanism.
claims.source: Importantly, it was reported that cycloheximide treatment also abolishes Hsf1 activity in mammalian cell by an unknown mechanism (Santagata et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Santagata et al., 2013.

claims.claim: A dynamic balance between unassembled and assembled RPs could be sensed by Hsf1 to constantly adjust protein homeostasis transcription programs in eukaryotes with translational flux, proteolysis and the rate of ribosome assembly.
claims.source: We propose that a dynamic balance between unassembled and assembled RPs could be sensed by Hsf1 to constantly adjust protein homeostasis transcription programs in eukaryotes with translational flux, proteolysis and the rate of ribosome assembly (Figure 8), since disruption or hyperactivation of any of these processes will rapidly change nuclear levels of free RPs.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on experimental findings.

results.result: Top1 depletion triggers a rapid, transient, and highly specific transcriptional response characterized by upregulation of Hsf1 target genes and downregulation of RP genes. This response is dependent on Hsf1 for stress gene activation but independent of Hsf1 for RP gene repression, and involves rapid release of Ifh1 from RP gene promoters.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C28 are well-supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 1A-G) showing specific transcriptional changes, transient kinetics, Top2-dependent re-equilibration, Ifh1 release from RP promoters, and Hsf1-dependent stress gene activation. The experimental design includes appropriate controls and the conclusions are directly supported by the data.

results.result: Top1 depletion causes proteotoxic stress in the nucleus by disrupting rRNA synthesis and ribosome assembly, leading to accumulation of unassembled ribosomal proteins in insoluble fractions and trailing polysome gradient fractions.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C39 are supported by multiple lines of evidence including microscopy showing Btn2 foci and Pre6 accumulation (Figure 2—supplement 1A,B), pulse-labeling showing reduced pre-rRNA synthesis (Figure 2—supplement 1C), Northern blots showing truncated pre-rRNAs (Figure 2A), polysome profiles showing 60S/40S imbalance (Figure 2B-C), and biochemical fractionation showing RP accumulation in insoluble fractions (Figure 2D). The convergent evidence strongly supports the conclusion.

results.result: Multiple perturbations to ribosome biogenesis (depletion of Utp8, Utp13, or treatment with diazaborine) trigger the same transcriptional response as Top1 depletion, termed RASTR (Ribosome Assembly Stress Response).
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C47 are supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 2E-G) showing that different perturbations at various steps of ribosome biogenesis (rRNA transcription, 40S processing, 60S maturation) all produce similar transcriptional responses. The consistency across different perturbations strongly supports the existence of a unified RASTR pathway.

results.result: RASTR is independent of the Ribosome Quality Control (RQC) pathway, as deletion of TAE2 does not affect RASTR activation, indicating distinct mechanisms for responding to ribosome assembly versus ribosome activity defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C53 are supported by experimental data (Figure 2—supplement 1D) showing that tae2Δ cells retain normal RASTR responses. This is a critical control experiment that distinguishes RASTR from the previously described RQC pathway and is well-supported by the data.

results.result: Ifh1 regulation during RASTR differs from TORC1 inhibition: ifh1-ΔC shows stable promoter release during Top1 depletion, RP gene repression and Hsf1 activation occur with identical kinetics, and Ifh1 concentrates in nuclear foci after topoisomerase depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C59 are supported by ChIP data (Figure 3A), kinetic analysis (Figure 3B), and microscopy (Figure 3C). The data demonstrate distinct temporal mechanisms of Ifh1 regulation and suggest sensitivity to unassembled RPs. The experimental evidence is clear and the conclusions are well-justified.

results.result: In cells lacking the E3 ligase Tom1, Ifh1 accumulates in nuclear foci even without stress, and tom1Δ is synthetically lethal with ifh1-AA but not ifh1-6, suggesting that RP aggregation directly impacts Ifh1 promoter binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C63 are supported by microscopy data (Figure 3D) and genetic interaction data (Figure 3E). The synthetic lethality pattern specifically links Tom1 function to Ifh1 promoter binding ability, providing strong genetic evidence for the proposed mechanism. The control with ifh1-6 strengthens the interpretation.

results.result: Mass spectrometry analysis of insoluble fractions following topoisomerase depletion reveals enrichment of chaperones, RPs, and RiBi factors (especially those for 60S biogenesis), with Ifh1 detected only after stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C66 are supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 3F-G, Supplementary file 3). The proteomic analysis provides comprehensive evidence for protein accumulation in insoluble fractions during RASTR. The detection of Ifh1 only after stress is a key finding that supports the sequestration model.

results.result: Ifh1 depletion by anchor-away leads to specific downregulation of RP genes and aberrant rRNA processing, and abolishes or strongly reduces Hsf1 target gene activation during topoisomerase depletion, demonstrating that RP production is required for Hsf1 activation during RASTR.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C72 are supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 4B, 4E-G), Northern blots (Figure 4C), and the observation that Ifh1 depletion alone downregulates Hsf1 targets (Figure 4D). The convergent evidence from multiple experiments strongly supports the conclusion that RP production is required for RASTR.

results.result: Cycloheximide treatment, which blocks translation and depletes nuclear RP pools, triggers a transcriptional response opposite to RASTR (Hsf1 target gene downregulation, RP gene upregulation) and completely abolishes RASTR when combined with topoisomerase depletion, demonstrating that RASTR depends on de novo protein synthesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C78 are supported by Northern blots (Figure 5B), ChIP-seq data (Figure 5C-E), and the striking observation of opposite transcriptional responses. The cycloheximide experiments provide critical evidence that de novo RP synthesis is required for RASTR and suggest that even unstressed cells balance RP production with Hsf1 activity.

results.result: Cycloheximide prevents RP aggregation, reduces Ifh1 nuclear foci in tom1Δ cells, increases Ifh1 promoter binding, prevents Ifh1 release during RASTR, and abolishes accumulation of RP and Ifh1 nuclear aggregates during RASTR.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C83 are supported by microscopy data (Figure 5F-G, Figure 5—supplement 1B, E-F) and ChIP data (Figure 5—supplement 1C-D). These experiments demonstrate the dynamic nature of RP and Ifh1 aggregates and their dependence on ongoing protein synthesis, providing strong mechanistic insights.

results.result: Newly synthesized RPs operate as a central hub coordinating RP gene expression with Hsf1-dependent activation of chaperone and proteasome genes in both stressed and unstressed cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C84 is a synthesis of multiple experimental results (Ifh1 depletion and cycloheximide experiments) and represents a well-supported integrative conclusion. The data from Figures 4 and 5 collectively support this model of RP-mediated coordination of transcriptional programs.

results.result: RASTR is the initial transcriptional response to TORC1 inhibition by rapamycin: Hsf1 targets are transiently upregulated at 5 min then downregulated at 20 min, and cycloheximide pre-treatment prevents the early (5 min) but not late (20 min) response, consistent with a two-step mechanism of RP gene regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C91 are supported by Northern blots (Figure 6A), ChIP-seq data (Figure 6B-E), and ChIP data (Figure 6F). The temporal analysis and cycloheximide experiments clearly demonstrate biphasic regulation and link the early phase to RASTR. This integrates RASTR into the broader stress response framework.

results.result: Heat shock triggers rapid RP gene downregulation that is prevented by cycloheximide pre-treatment, while Hsf1 target genes remain activated even with cycloheximide, suggesting RASTR plays an integral role in the heat-shock response and may constitute the earliest RNAPII transcriptional response to various stress conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 are supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 7A-C) showing differential effects of cycloheximide on RP versus Hsf1 target genes during heat shock. The data demonstrate that RASTR contributes to heat shock response, though C95's speculation about generality to other stresses is appropriately cautious.

results.result: RASTR is a novel regulatory pathway providing rapid, specific coordination of protein homeostasis and RP gene expression during ribosome assembly disruption, requiring neo-synthesis of RPs and involving RP aggregates that activate Hsf1 (proposed via chaperone competition) and sequester Ifh1.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C101 represent the core conclusions of the study. C96-C99 are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data. C100 (chaperone competition mechanism) is appropriately presented as a proposal based on inference, though direct evidence for this specific mechanism is limited. C101 (Ifh1 sequestration) is well-supported by the mass spectrometry and microscopy data.

results.result: Cycloheximide treatment produces opposite transcriptional effects to RASTR, supporting a model where unstressed cells constantly monitor nuclear unassembled RP levels to balance Hsf1 and RP gene expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C103 are supported by the cycloheximide experiments (Figure 5C). C102 is directly demonstrated by data, while C103 represents a well-reasoned model based on the experimental observations. The model is appropriately presented as a proposal.

results.result: RASTR is the initial transcriptional response to TORC1 inactivation, and disequilibrium at any step in ribosome biogenesis leads to RASTR activation until unassembled RP pools decrease.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 are supported by the rapamycin experiments (Figure 6) and the multiple perturbation experiments (Figure 2E-G). The data demonstrate that RASTR responds to various ribosome biogenesis defects and represents an early response to TORC1 inhibition.

results.result: RPs are abundant ubiquitinated proteins in proteasome-deficient cells, accumulate rapidly in insoluble fractions during ribosome assembly stress, and blocking RP production diminishes Hsf1 activation, suggesting RP aggregates are important RASTR signals. Additional proteins including RiBi factors, Ifh1, and chaperones also accumulate, and these aggregates are highly dynamic.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C111 integrate data from mass spectrometry (Figure 3F-G), biochemical fractionation (Figure 2D), Ifh1/cycloheximide experiments (Figures 4-5), and kinetic analyses (Figure 1). The evidence strongly supports the role of RP aggregates in RASTR signaling and demonstrates the dynamic nature of these structures.

results.result: S. cerevisiae has developed temporally distinct mechanisms to regulate RP gene expression: a short timescale mechanism (RASTR) resulting from rapid accumulation of unassembled RPs, and a long timescale mechanism. The rapid RASTR response helps clear proteotoxic unassembled RPs by inducing Hsf1 targets and arresting RP transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C117 synthesize findings from this study with prior work (Albert et al., 2016). C115 is supported by citations and current data. C116 is a well-reasoned mechanistic proposal based on the experimental evidence. C117 is appropriately presented as a proposed mechanism for how RASTR resolves the stress condition.

results.result: Hsf1 activity is tightly linked to ribosome biogenesis in yeast independent of RQC, and a dynamic balance between unassembled and assembled RPs could be sensed by Hsf1 to adjust protein homeostasis programs with translational flux, proteolysis, and ribosome assembly rates.
results.evaluation: Claim C125 is supported by the current experimental data and comparison with Tye et al. (2018). Claim C129 represents a well-reasoned model based on the comprehensive experimental evidence, appropriately presented as a proposal. The model integrates multiple observations into a coherent framework.

results.result: Ribosome biogenesis is a complex, energy-demanding process requiring coordination of rRNA and RP production. Rapidly growing yeast produce ~2000 ribosomes/minute, requiring assembly of 4 rRNAs with 79 RPs that are highly prone to aggregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations (Warner, 1999; David et al., 2010; Pillet et al., 2017; Rand and Grant, 2006; Weids et al., 2016). These provide essential context for the study.

results.result: Unassembled RPs activate p53 in metazoans through MDM2 titration, but yeast lack p53. Hsf1 is a central regulator of proteostasis in eukaryotes, is essential in yeast and malignant cells, and drives expression of chaperones, aggregases, and proteasome components.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C10 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These claims provide important context about p53-independent pathways and Hsf1 function that motivates the study.

results.result: The RQC complex (conserved from yeast to human) increases Hsf1 activity under translation stress. ERISQ specifically recognizes unassembled RPs in the nucleus for proteasome degradation, with Tom1 ubiquitin ligase preventing accumulation of insoluble RPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C15 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations (Brandman et al., 2012; Sung et al., 2016a,b; Gorenstein and Warner, 1977; Warner, 1977). These provide important context about existing quality control mechanisms.

results.result: Decreased ribosome abundance protects against proteotoxic stress. RP gene transcription is regulated by Ifh1, which is rapidly released from promoters upon TORC1 inhibition and coordinated with RNAPI activity during prolonged inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C19 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide essential context about RP gene regulation and motivate the investigation of rapid Ifh1 release mechanisms.

results.result: Newly synthesized unassembled RPs accumulate in aggregates during ribosome assembly stress. The RQC binds 60S subunits with stalled polypeptides, triggers their degradation, and activates Hsf1 targets; cells lacking Tae2 fail to activate Hsf1 after translational stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C38, C48-C50 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context about RP aggregation and the RQC pathway that is distinguished from RASTR.

results.result: Top1 was identified through a mak1 mutation defective in 60S production and is required for rRNA synthesis. Utp8 (t-UTP subcomplex) depletion inhibits rDNA transcription; Utp13 (UTP-B) depletion affects 40S synthesis; diazaborine inhibits Drg1 and blocks 60S maturation.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C32, C43-C47 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context about the tools used to perturb ribosome biogenesis at different steps.

results.result: Previous work established that Ifh1 is rapidly released from RP promoters upon TORC1 inhibition, with stable release requiring the C-terminal domain and CURI complex. In constitutively active RNAPI strains, Ifh1 returns to promoters unless sequestered by Utp22/Rrp7 in the CURI complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C55, C91, C113-C114 represent prior work from the authors' laboratory (Albert et al., 2016; Schawalder et al., 2004; Rudra et al., 2007) that provides essential context for understanding the current findings about RASTR.

results.result: Cycloheximide blocks translation and depletes nuclear RP pools, prevents RP aggregation after proteasome inhibition, and RP production ceases ~15 min after rapamycin treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C73, C79, C88 represent established knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context for interpreting the cycloheximide experiments in the current study.

results.result: Nucleolar proteins can form liquid-liquid phase separated structures. In higher eukaryotes, ribosome assembly stress in ribosomopathies may involve unassembled RPs triggering feedback to decrease ribosome biogenesis gene transcription via c-Myc inhibition and p53 activation. DDX21 helicase activates RP promoters in a manner sensitive to ribosome biogenesis status.
results.evaluation: Claims C112, C118-C121 represent established knowledge and hypotheses from the literature supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context for discussing potential conservation and mechanisms in higher eukaryotes.

results.result: Hsf1 is a conserved sensor of proteotoxic stress controlling chaperones, reduces protein aggregates in neurodegenerative diseases, and promotes proteostasis in tumor cells. In mammalian cells, RPs have high turnover, accumulate in the nucleus upon proteasome/ribosome assembly inhibition, and cycloheximide abolishes Hsf1 activity by unknown mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C124, C126-C128 represent established knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context for discussing potential conservation of RASTR mechanisms in mammals.
